## FAQ (Expanded)
Q: What are varicose veins?
A: Varicose veins are enlarged surface veins where one-way valves fail, allowing blood to pool. They can cause pain, swelling, and complications if untreated.

Q: Will I be seen personally by one of the Schulman doctors?
A: Yes. Every patient is seen and treated by Dr. Martin L. Schulman or Dr. Lee G. Schulman.

Q: Does insurance cover vein treatment?
A: Coverage depends on plan and diagnosis. EVLT for medical varicose disease is often covered. Cosmetic treatments are typically not covered.

Q: Am I awake during vein treatments?
A: Yes. Treatments are performed under local anesthesia, and patients typically walk and drive home the same day.

Q: How many treatments will I need?
A: Many patients improve in one or two visits, but exact treatment count depends on severity and vein distribution.

Q: Is vein stripping surgery still done?
A: Modern EVLT and related minimally invasive techniques have largely replaced vein stripping.

Q: Can varicose veins come back after treatment?
A: Treated veins stay closed, but new veins can develop over time because vein disease is often hereditary.

Q: Do you treat veins outside the legs?
A: Yes. Treatments include hand, facial, temple, chest, breast, arm, and other body veins.

Q: What is the difference between spider veins and varicose veins?
A: Varicose veins are larger bulging veins with medical symptoms; spider veins are smaller superficial vessels, often cosmetic.

Q: What can I expect on my first visit?
A: First visits include history, exam, and Doppler ultrasound when indicated, followed by a clear treatment plan.

## Insurance & Payment
- The center works with patient insurance plans and submits clinical documentation when medical treatment is indicated.
- EVLT for medically necessary varicose vein treatment is often eligible for coverage.
- Cosmetic vein treatments are commonly self-pay.
- For patients without coverage, fee reductions and payment plans may be available.
